modern: Death is a ceasing of the impressions through the senses, and of the pulling of the strings which move the appetites, and of the wandering movements of the thoughts, and of the service to the flesh.
original: Death is a cessation of the impressions through the senses, and of the pulling of the strings which move the appetites, and of the discursive movements of the thoughts, and of the service to the flesh.

explained.summary: Death is the end of the senses pulling at you, of desires jerking you around like strings on a puppet, of thoughts wandering off in all directions, and of having to look after the body. Marcus describes it as a kind of rest from all the things that keep a person busy and unsettled, without fear or drama.
